name: TopK + ConE (Revisiting Demonstration Selection Strategies in In-Context Learning)
venue: ACL 2024 (Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, Long Papers, pp. 9090-9101)
authors_affiliation: Keqin Peng (Beihang University), Liang Ding (The University of Sydney), Yancheng Yuan (The Hong Kong Polytechnic University), Xuebo Liu (Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen), Min Zhang (Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen), Yuanxin Ouyang (Beihang University), Dacheng Tao (Nanyang Technological University). Corresponding authors: Liang Ding and Yancheng Yuan.
task_domain: In-context learning (ICL) demonstration selection for NLP: natural language understanding (text classification, NLI) and natural language generation (machine translation).
problem_setting: Offline, single-model, single-turn ICL with no additional training of the inference model or retriever. Given a labeled demonstration pool and a test input, the goal is to select k few-shot demonstrations that maximize ICL task performance. The authors first empirically show ICL demonstration choice is both data-dependent and model-dependent (it varies with the retrieval module and, critically, with the inference model), then propose a training-free, model-dependent selection-then-rerank recipe. Supervision: the demonstration pool has gold labels; no preference labels or RL training are used. The inference model itself scores candidates (self-scoring via its own likelihood/cross-entropy).
what_is_retrieved: Demonstrations (labeled input-output examples / few-shot exemplars) drawn from a training-set demonstration pool.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: a fixed labeled demonstration pool (training set), e.g., SST-2/SST-5/CR/Subj/AGNews/MNLI/QNLI training data, or Flores-200 / WMT22 parallel data for translation. No agent-written growing memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k selection (k-shot, with k = 4 for GPT2-XL and k = 8 for other models). The contribution is a model-dependent reranking objective (minimize conditional entropy of the test input) layered on top of a fixed-size top-k retrieval, not a completeness-recovery or variable-size objective.
retrieval_unit: Single demonstration (a complete input-output / problem-solution example). Demonstrations are individually scored and combined into a k-shot group.
index_source: Static corpus, offline-induced: the retrievable store is the fixed labeled training pool. No online/test-time growth; candidate scores are computed at test time per test sample but the store itself is frozen.
index_structure_topology: Flat dense vector index for the TopK selection stage (sentence-transformer embeddings, nearest-neighbor search); no graph/hierarchical/cluster topology. The ConE reranking stage scores candidates directly with the inference model rather than via an index.
retriever_type: Hybrid two-stage: (1) selection module = dense retriever (TopK / SBERT cosine nearest neighbors) by default, optionally BM25 or Random; (2) reranking module = LLM-as-scorer using the inference model's own conditional-entropy estimate (ConE). The proposed default is TopK (dense) + ConE.
retriever_learning_signal: None / off-the-shelf for the selection stage (pretrained sentence-transformer embeddings; no contrastive fine-tuning of the retriever). The ConE reranker is a training-free, model-dependent score (conditional entropy / cross-entropy estimated by the frozen inference model itself); no learning signal, no RL, no preference labels.
query_construction: Raw test input used as the query for the TopK selection stage (nearest neighbors in embedding space). For ConE reranking, each candidate demonstration group c is combined with the raw test input x to form a prompt, and the inference model's conditional entropy H_theta(x|c) = H_theta(x,c) - H_theta(c) is computed.
query_granularity: Task-level / per-test-sample one-shot retrieval (a single retrieval+rerank pass is done once for each test input before generating its answer); not step-level or trajectory-level.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot: a single retrieval (TopK selection) followed by a single rerank (ConE) is performed once per test sample before inference. No iterative or uncertainty-triggered re-retrieval.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval is always performed once per test sample (not conditioned on confidence, attention, or a learned router). The ConE score itself is an entropy/uncertainty signal but it is used for ranking, not for triggering when to retrieve.
reranking: Yes. The core contribution is the ConE reranking stage: TopK retrieves 30 candidates, then candidates are ranked by the inference model's conditional entropy of the test input H_theta(x|c) (lower entropy = better understanding = higher rank). This is a model-dependent, self-scoring reranker (a likelihood/entropy-based reranker rather than a trained cross-encoder).
retrieved_context_refinement: Rerank only: candidates from TopK are re-ranked by ConE; no decomposition, compression, distractor filtering, or distillation of the demonstration text.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: the selected k demonstrations are concatenated as few-shot exemplars in the inference model's prompt; the model then performs the task (classification label or translation) via standard ICL.
planning_integration: One-shot exemplars at inference time. There is no planning/acting/tree-search component; retrieval feeds a single-pass ICL prediction (retrieve-then-rerank-then-prompt). Not applicable to multi-step planning.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer: retrieval and reranking happen once per test query, before producing the single final answer. No per-step or per-token interleaving.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw demonstration (verbatim labeled input-output example) injected as a few-shot exemplar in the prompt; no distillation, abstraction, or latent encoding of the demonstration.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Single demonstration (raw labeled example); no distilled strategy, guideline, workflow, or skill.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Model-dependent self-scoring as an implicit relevance/quality evaluator: ConE selects demonstrations that most reduce the inference model's conditional entropy on the test input, favoring demonstrations the model can actually leverage. The authors also show the method reduces sensitivity to demonstration order (smaller variance than Random/TopK). No retriever-aware training or explicit distractor-filtering.
memory_type: none (a static labeled demonstration pool; no episodic/skill/workflow/procedural/graph/latent memory).
write_back: false. The system does not store new experiences/cases/skills; the demonstration pool is fixed and read-only.
online_growth: false. The retrievable store does not grow at deployment/test time; it is the frozen training pool.
failure_experience_usage: N/A. No failed/negative experiences are stored or retrieved; demonstrations are gold-labeled training examples (success-only by construction, but there is no experience-collection loop).
memory_evolution_update: N/A (no stored entries are mutated; the pool is static).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: false. Selection is fixed similarity top-k plus a training-free conditional-entropy rerank; no learned/RL-optimized retrieval policy (no M-MDP, no soft Q-learning, no preference training).
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: N/A / single-model private use; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory sharing.
benchmarks: NLU: SST-2, SST-5, CR, Subj, AGNews, MNLI, QNLI (7 classification/NLI tasks). NLG (machine translation): 4 language pairs extracted from Flores-200 (1012 examples per language; reported pairs include En<->X and non-English-centric Ru<=>De), plus WMT22 mixed-domain translation (e-commerce, news, social; including Zh=>En). Inference models: GPT2-XL (1.5B), Llama2-7B, Llama2-13B, and aligned chat models (Vicuna, LLaMA-chat, DeepSeek-chat). Retrieval embedding models for the analysis: all-MiniLM-L6-v2, all-MiniLM-L12-v2, all-distilroberta-v1, all-mpnet-base-v2.
benchmark_family: QA/NLU text classification and NLI (SST-2/SST-5/CR/Subj/AGNews/MNLI/QNLI) + machine-translation generation (Flores-200, WMT22). Not a planning/web/embodied/tool/code/agent-memory benchmark family.
baselines: Prompting (zero-shot, no demonstrations), Random, BM25 (Robertson et al. 2009), TopK (Liu et al. 2022, dense nearest-neighbor selection), and TopK + MDL (Wu et al. 2023b, select-then-rank by Minimum Description Length). TopK + MDL is the prior state-of-the-art comparison.
key_metrics: Accuracy for classification/NLI tasks; COMET (reference-based COMET-20 = wmt20-COMET-da and COMET-22 = wmt22-COMET-da) for translation, with comet-compare significance testing (p<0.05). Conditional entropy of the test input is used as an analysis metric to explain why methods work.
headline_result: On Llama2-7B across 7 NLU tasks, TopK + ConE (Ours) reaches 77.9 average accuracy, vs 76.7 for TopK+MDL (+1.2), 76.1 for TopK (+1.8), 75.0 for BM25 (+2.9), 71.2 for Random (+6.8), and 56.0 for Prompting (+21.9). Largest single-task gains over the previous best are Subj +4.6% and QNLI +1.9%.
ablations: 1) ConE is complementary to any selection method: adding ConE to Random/BM25/TopK improves all of them (e.g., +7.5 on SST-2 with Random selection), motivating TopK+ConE as the default. 2) Number of in-context examples N swept 0->16: more demonstrations generally help but GPT2-XL degrades beyond its max length, so N=4 for GPT2-XL and N=8 for others; ConE consistently beats TopK across N. 3) Number of TopK candidates reranked by ConE: more candidates improve performance; default set to 30. 4) Model-scale sweep (GPT2-XL 1.5B to Llama2-13B): consistent gains, with GPT2-XL gaining +2.6% over TopK+MDL and +3.6% over TopK. 5) Order sensitivity: TopK+ConE has higher average and smaller variance than Random/TopK under demonstration-order shuffling. 6) Universality: prior methods (BM25/TopK/MDL) also reduce conditional entropy of test inputs, giving a unified explanation. 7) Works for instruction-tuned/RLHF chat models (Vicuna, LLaMA-chat, DeepSeek-chat) and mixed-domain translation pools.
evaluation_decoupling: No separate intrinsic retrieval metrics (no Recall@k/nDCG). Evaluation is end-to-end task performance (accuracy / COMET). Conditional entropy of the test input is reported as an explanatory/analysis quantity rather than a decoupled retrieval-quality metric.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome metrics (final accuracy / COMET). The only process-level quantity analyzed is the conditional entropy of the test input (used to explain mechanism and order-robustness variance), not stepwise reasoning or retrieval-accuracy scoring.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: ConE adds inference-time cost: for each test sample, the inference model must score (forward-pass) 30 TopK candidates to compute conditional entropy, then run final inference. The TopK selection stage narrows the candidate pool to make this feasible (vs enumerating all combinations, which is intractable). The authors note this added inference budget may be unacceptable for extremely large LLMs and flag a more efficient understanding-measure as future work. No explicit latency/throughput numbers are reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k injection: k = 4 demonstrations for GPT2-XL (limited by max sequence length), k = 8 for Llama2-7B/13B and chat models. Candidate set = 30 (TopK retrieves 30, ConE reranks and selects the final k). Budget effectively capped by model max length (GPT2-XL degrades when forced to 8-shot).
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (this is a method paper, not a survey).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing public benchmarks; Flores-200 contributes 1012 examples per language pair). Not a benchmark-construction paper.
builds_on: TopK (Liu et al. 2022, KATE / k-nearest-neighbor dense demonstration retrieval); the select-then-rank framework and MDL reranking of Wu et al. (2023b); OpenICL toolkit (Wu et al. 2023a) for the codebase; Gonen et al. (2023) perplexity/familiarity insight (model performs better on prompts it is more familiar with) motivating the conditional-entropy conjecture; BM25 (Robertson et al. 2009).
contrasts_with: Purely data-dependent similarity heuristics (BM25, TopK) that ignore the inference model; TopK + MDL (Wu et al. 2023b) which reranks by Minimum Description Length rather than by the model's conditional entropy of the test input; Random and zero-shot Prompting. The key contrast is data-only vs data-and-model-dependent selection.
lineage: Group A (ICL demonstration retrieval / selection). Sits in the demonstration-selection lineage from KATE/TopK (similarity-based) -> TopK+MDL (likelihood/MDL reranking) -> TopK+ConE (model-dependent conditional-entropy reranking), and explicitly offers a unified conditional-entropy explanation for prior similarity-based and likelihood-based selection methods.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not a CBR method; at most a single Retrieve phase, no Reuse/Revise/Retain in the CBR sense).
explicit_cbr_grounding: false. The paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it is framed as ICL demonstration selection.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tools/skills; demonstrations are raw labeled examples indexed by sentence-transformer embeddings).
index_content_separation: N/A (no lightweight-index-then-content separation; demonstrations are short examples retrieved and used directly).
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool index, no MCP/RapidAPI/function-calling protocol).
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (no case adaptation; retrieved demonstrations are used verbatim as ICL exemplars).
